# shadow/no-destructure-props-outside-forgiving

Disallow destructuring props where the compiler does not keep them reactive (autoReactive off, or an unsupported form).

`recommended` `has suggestions`

## Why

Props are getters: destructuring reads them once, so later updates never reach the destructured names. With `autoReactive` on (the default), the compiler rewrites `({ title }) => ...` and `const { title } = props` in components so each name follows `props`. That rewrite only covers PascalCase components declared directly, with one parameter, top-level `const` declarations and plain patterns. Everywhere else the destructuring silently freezes the value; this rule reports exactly those places. Set `autoReactive: false` to report every destructuring (for projects that compile with `autoReactive: false`).

## Incorrect

```tsx
function Row({ id, ...rest }) {
  return <li data-id={id} {...rest} />;
}
```

```tsx
function Row(props) {
  let { title } = props;
  return <li>{title}</li>;
}
```

```tsx
function Row(props) {
  if (props.on) {
    const { title } = props;
    log(title);
  }
  return <li />;
}
```

```tsx
const Row = memo(({ title }) => <li>{title}</li>);
```

## Correct

```tsx
function Row({ id, title = 'untitled' }) {
  return <li data-id={id}>{title}</li>;
}
```

```tsx
function Row(props) {
  const { title } = props;
  return <li>{title}</li>;
}
```

```tsx
function Row(props) {
  const [local, rest] = splitProps(props, ['id']);
  return <li data-id={local.id} {...rest} />;
}
```

## Options

```json
[
  {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "autoReactive": {
        "type": "boolean"
      }
    },
    "additionalProperties": false
  }
]
```

Defaults: `[{"autoReactive":true}]`

## Suggestions

The suggestion reads props directly: a parameter pattern becomes `props` (keeping its type annotation) or a `const { a } = props` declaration is removed, and every read of a destructured name becomes `props.key` (with the component's own parameter name in the declaration case). It is withheld for patterns with defaults, rest elements, nesting or computed keys, when a destructured name is reassigned, when the component already has a binding named `props` (parameter case), when a nested scope or an outer binding would capture the rewritten name, when a comment sits inside the replaced text, and when the declaration declares more than one pattern or is not a statement of its own.

## Disabling

Disable one line with `// eslint-disable-next-line shadow/no-destructure-props-outside-forgiving`, a block with `/* eslint-disable shadow/no-destructure-props-outside-forgiving */` and `/* eslint-enable shadow/no-destructure-props-outside-forgiving */`, or a whole file with the block form at its top. Disable it when reading the props once is intended, for example an initial value that must not follow later updates.

## Notes

- Destructuring inside a callback that runs later (an effect, a memo, an event handler) reads the props at that time and is not reported.
- Option `autoReactive` (default `true`) mirrors the compiler flag of the same name.
- Suggestions rewrite plain patterns without defaults to `props.name`; patterns with defaults, rest or nesting need a manual change.

## Messages

- `frozenParam`: Destructuring props in the parameter list reads each prop once, so updates are lost ({{reason}}). Read `props.x` where it is used, or enable `autoReactive`.
- `frozenDeclaration`: Destructuring `{{props}}` reads each prop once, so updates are lost ({{reason}}). Read `{{props}}.x` where it is used, or enable `autoReactive`.
- `useProps`: Read `props.x` instead of destructuring.

## Configs

| Config | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| `recommended` | warn |
| `strict` | error ({"autoReactive":true}) |
| `migration` | warn |
| `dusk` | warn |
